Business goal: Create a new protected system root role with a stable machine key plus editable display name and description.
User outcome: A root operator can add a new reusable root role without editing code directly.
Notes / constraints: Clients may supply roleKey, displayName, and description only. RoleKey must be stable and unique. RootUserAdmin remains protected from day one.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Body includes roleKey, displayName, description, optional active flag defaulting to active. System-managed ids and audit fields are rejected.
Response contract: Returns created system root role with identifiers, lifecycle state, timestamps, and protected/mandatory metadata.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.create; 409 normalized roleKey already exists; 422 protected-role rule violation.
Persistence impact: Create durable system root role record.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique normalized active roleKey; durable primary key.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Backward-compatible additive feature. Seed RootUserAdmin via bootstrap/migration path rather than manual API creation.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Role creation must not allow duplicate normalized role keys or creation of malformed protected-role metadata.

Business goal: Read one system root role, including metadata and assigned capability summary.
User outcome: A root operator can inspect a role before editing it.
Notes / constraints: Should include stable roleKey, displayName, description, active/deleted status, assignable status, protected flags, and assigned capability summary.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Response contract: Returns one role plus assigned capability summary and lifecycle fields.
Error contract: 400 invalid id; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.read; 404 role not found.
Persistence impact: Read existing system root role and linked capability grants.
Indexes / uniqueness: Lookup by primary key; normalized roleKey index supports secondary reads.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Should preserve ability to expose protected-role metadata consistently in future UI/API consumers.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Response should clearly distinguish protected/mandatory grants from editable grants.

Business goal: List system root roles with descriptions, lifecycle state, and capability summary.
User outcome: A root operator can browse and select a role to inspect or edit.
Notes / constraints: Use standard list defaults: page=1, pageSize=25, pageSize max=100, default order desc. Exclude deleted rows by default unless explicit includeDeleted filter is later approved. Roles should expose whether they are assignable.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Supports standard pagination plus optional filters for active/protected and search by normalized roleKey/displayName if approved.
Response contract: Returns paginated list shape with items and metadata.
Error contract: 400 invalid paging/filter input; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.list.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes should support normalized roleKey/displayName list filters if enabled.
Search / filter model: Paginated list with optional active/protected filters; no deleted rows by default.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Follow current repo list conventions for consistent rebuild-from-spec behavior.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: List behavior should match current shared pagination defaults and exclude deleted roles by default.

Business goal: Update editable system root role metadata without changing the stable machine key.
User outcome: A root operator can refine how a role is presented and described over time.
Notes / constraints: Editable fields are displayName and description. roleKey remains immutable after creation. Protected roles can still have presentation metadata updated unless later restricted.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootRoleId required; body permits displayName and description only.
Response contract: Returns updated role with refreshed updatedAt.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.update; 404 role not found; 409 normalized display conflict if such uniqueness is later adopted.
Persistence impact: Update durable role metadata and updatedAt.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique roleKey remains unchanged; no client override of lifecycle/system fields.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Preserve stable role identity so assignments and audit history remain durable.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Updates must not allow roleKey mutation or silent lifecycle changes.

Business goal: Deactivate a system root role so it can no longer be newly assigned while preserving history and existing assignments.
User outcome: A root operator can retire a role from future use without losing historical correctness.
Notes / constraints: Soft delete/deactivate only. Do not hard delete. Protected roles such as RootUserAdmin cannot be deactivated if platform safety rules would be violated. Existing assignments may remain for history or controlled transition, but new assignments must be blocked once the role is inactive.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootRoleId required; optional reason/comment may be captured for audit.
Response contract: Returns deactivated role with deletedAt/updatedAt and lifecycle state showing it is no longer assignable.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.delete; 404 role not found; 409 protected-role or platform safety violation.
Persistence impact: Set deletedAt and updatedAt on role; preserve grants and historical/current assignment records durably.
Indexes / uniqueness: Active uniqueness on normalized roleKey should allow future reactivation but prevent duplicate active keys.
Search / filter model: Deleted roles excluded from normal lists and from assignable-role pickers by default.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Soft deletion chosen to preserve rebuild/compliance history while preventing future assignment of retired roles.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: System must block deactivation when it would leave no RootUserAdmin assigned or break protected platform safety rules, but should not require all existing assignments to be removed first.

Business goal: Restore a previously deactivated system root role.
User outcome: A root operator can bring back a retired role without recreating it or losing history.
Notes / constraints: Only valid for previously deactivated roles. Reactivation must respect unique active roleKey constraints.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Response contract: Returns reactivated role with cleared deletedAt and refreshed updatedAt.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.reactivate; 404 role not found; 409 role already active or active-key conflict.
Indexes / uniqueness: Must respect unique active normalized roleKey index on reactivation.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: First-class capability because delete semantics are deactivate-only.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Reactivation should restore the prior durable role identity and make the role assignable again without creating a new record.

Business goal: List the current eligible root authz capabilities that may be assigned to a system root role.
User outcome: A root operator can see the capability catalog when editing a role.
Notes / constraints: This is the authoritative catalog-backed list for root-role editing. Non-assigned capabilities can be derived by comparing this result with assigned grants.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootRoleId required; standard pagination/filtering may apply if capability catalog grows.
Response contract: Returns paginated eligible capability list with key, description, protected flag, mandatory-for-role indicator if applicable, and lifecycle status.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.capability-catalog.read; 404 role not found.
Persistence impact: Read from durable/root capability catalog plus role context.
Indexes / uniqueness: Capability catalog keyed by unique capability key.
Search / filter model: Paginated list with optional filters for protected/mandatory/active capability states.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Capability catalog route uses explicit authz naming to avoid confusion with unrelated eligible lists elsewhere in the platform.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Catalog must include enough metadata to explain what each capability does and whether it is mandatory for the selected role.

Business goal: List which authz capabilities are currently assigned to a system root role.
User outcome: A root operator can review the role’s current grants before changing them.
Notes / constraints: Should distinguish protected and mandatory grants from optional grants and include grant source metadata where relevant.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootRoleId required; standard pagination/filtering may apply if grant count grows.
Response contract: Returns assigned capability grants with capability metadata and protected/mandatory indicators.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.capability-assignment.read; 404 role not found.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique active assignment per role/capability pair.
Search / filter model: Paginated list with optional protected/mandatory filters.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Assigned/non-assigned split should be derivable consistently from the eligible catalog plus assignment records.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Returned assignments must make it obvious which grants cannot be removed.

Business goal: Change the capability grants assigned to a system root role.
User outcome: A root operator can bulk-manage a role’s grants and later support drag-and-drop UI workflows.
Notes / constraints: Bulk set/replace is the priority model; future incremental add/remove routes may be added without replacing this capability. Mandatory/protected grants cannot be removed.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootRoleId required; body contains desired capability key set plus optional reason/comment. System validates keys against eligible root capability catalog.
Response contract: Returns updated assigned capability set plus protected/mandatory markers.
Error contract: 400 invalid payload; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.capability-assignment.update; 404 role not found; 409 attempted removal of mandatory/protected grant or invalid catalog transition.
Persistence impact: Upsert/delete role-to-capability assignment records and audit before/after grant sets.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique active assignment per role/capability pair; indexes support role grant reads.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow.
Compatibility / migration notes: Bulk-first contract chosen so future UI can submit the full selected set deterministically.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Server must reject any update that would strip required RootUserAdmin grants or leave the role without its protected identity.

Business goal: Assign a system root role to a root user.
User outcome: A root operator can grant additional root capabilities to another operator.
Notes / constraints: A root user may hold multiple roles. Assignments take effect immediately. Inactive/deactivated roles cannot be newly assigned.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootUserId required; body includes rootRoleId plus optional reason/comment. Bulk assignment is not needed here because the operation is one assignment at a time.
Response contract: Returns created assignment record and refreshed effective permission summary for the target root user or enough identifiers to fetch it.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.assignment.assign; 404 root user or role not found; 409 assignment already exists or role inactive.
Cross-feature seams: rootUsers public read seam for target root user existence and lifecycle checks.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique active assignment per rootUser/role pair.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and rootUsers feature seam.
Compatibility / migration notes: Cross-feature read/write must use rootUsers public seam rather than direct persistence imports.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; ties authorization state to an identifiable operator account.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Assignment must not target deleted/ineligible root users and must reject inactive roles.

Business goal: Remove a system root role from a root user while preserving safety constraints and audit history.
User outcome: A root operator can reduce or revoke another operator’s access safely.
Notes / constraints: Must not leave a root user with zero roles. Must not leave the platform with zero RootUserAdmin assignments. Multiple roles remain supported.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.

Response contract: Returns deactivated assignment record and refreshed effective permission summary for the target root user or enough identifiers to fetch it.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.assignment.unassign; 404 assignment not found; 409 would leave target root user with zero roles or platform with no RootUserAdmin assignment.
Cross-feature seams: rootUsers public read seam for target root user lifecycle and existence checks.

Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and rootUsers feature seam.
Compatibility / migration notes: Safety rules are part of the durable contract and should not be left to UI-only enforcement.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; ties authorization state to an identifiable operator account.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Server must block any unassignment that violates minimum-role or last-RootUserAdmin safety rules.

Business goal: List the system root roles currently assigned to a root user.
User outcome: A root operator can inspect role membership for a given root user before changing it.
Notes / constraints: Standard list rules apply. Include role metadata and assignment lifecycle summary.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootUserId required; standard pagination/filtering if needed.
Response contract: Returns paginated assigned role list with role metadata and assignment metadata.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.assignment.list; 404 root user not found.
Cross-feature seams: rootUsers public read seam for target root user existence checks.
Persistence impact: Read assignment records joined to root role metadata.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes should support reads by rootUserId and active assignment state.
Search / filter model: Paginated list of active assignments by default.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and rootUsers feature seam.
Compatibility / migration notes: Should remain consistent with rootUsers lifecycle semantics and default list behavior.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; reveals authorization state for identifiable operator account.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Default listing should exclude inactive assignment records unless an explicit historical read is later added, but it may still show an assigned role whose role definition is now inactive.

Business goal: Replace one assigned system root role on a root user with another role in a single controlled operation.
User outcome: A root operator can migrate a user off an old role onto a new one without leaving them temporarily under-privileged or with zero roles.
Notes / constraints: Intended for controlled role evolution and retirement workflows. Operation should atomically add the replacement role and retire the old assignment. Replacement must not violate RootUserAdmin minimum-presence rules.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Request contract: Exact rootUserId required; body includes fromRootRoleAssignmentId or fromRootRoleId, toRootRoleId, and optional reason/comment. Operation must be atomic.
Response contract: Returns retired old assignment, created replacement assignment, and refreshed effective permission summary for the target root user.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.assignment.replace; 404 root user, source assignment, or target role not found; 409 replacement would violate minimum-role or protected-platform safety rules, or target role is inactive.
Cross-feature seams: rootUsers public read seam for target root user existence and lifecycle checks.
Persistence impact: Deactivate old assignment and create replacement assignment atomically while preserving durable audit history.
Indexes / uniqueness: Uses active uniqueness per rootUser/role pair plus assignment lifecycle fields; transaction boundaries must preserve safety invariants.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and rootUsers feature seam.
Compatibility / migration notes: Provides a deterministic lifecycle path for evolving root roles without forcing ad hoc unassign/reassign sequences.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Privacy / personal data impact: Moderate; ties authorization state to an identifiable operator account.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Replacement must be atomic and must never leave the target root user with zero roles or the platform with no RootUserAdmin assignment.

Business goal: Read the effective root permissions for a root user after all assigned roles are combined.
User outcome: A root operator can understand what another operator can actually do right now.
Notes / constraints: Return assigned roles, flattened effective capability set, and grant source explanation per capability.
Authorization summary: Protected root-role administration capability restricted to RootUserAdmin.
Frontend visibility rule: No tenant-facing surface. Future root-admin UI may expose this only to RootUserAdmin.
Backend enforcement rule: Enforce through central authorization seam using governing authz capability before feature service execution.
Response contract: Returns assigned roles, effective capability keys, protected/mandatory flags where relevant, and source role(s) for each grant.
Error contract: 400 invalid request; 401 unauthenticated; 403 missing root-role.effective-permissions.read; 404 root user not found.
Cross-feature seams: rootUsers public read seam for target root user existence checks; authorization seam for grant evaluation rules.
Persistence impact: Read root-user role assignments plus role-to-capability grants; dynamic effective-permission evaluation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes should support assignment and grant lookup paths used for effective-permission assembly.
Session / auth dependency: Depends on current rootAuth protected session flow and central authorization evaluation logic.
Compatibility / migration notes: Designed as an inspection endpoint so future additional root roles can be introduced without changing the concept of effective access.
Authorization enforcement layer: Central authorization seam at route/service boundary.
Audit requirement: Audit all successful mutations and any denied attempts with actor, target role/rootUser, before/after, timestamp, and reason where supplied.
Standards impact: OWASP ASVS authorization and audit controls; platform-status snapshots should be reviewed when implemented.
Acceptance notes: Effective access must be the union of positive grants across all assigned active role assignments and clearly show the source of each grant, even if a source role has since been retired from new assignment.
